name: qbc (Quick adaptive Binary Arithmetic Coder)
baseline: Quake 3 / ioquake3 adaptive Huffman Huff_Compress()/Huff_Decompress() (~50k memory)
workload: Compression of connect-command infostrings with a 0-order adaptive binary model, versus the engine's Huff_ functions; no corpus or sizes stated.
claimed_speedup: encode/decode speed about 20% faster; compression rate about 10% better; memory more than 50 times lower (<1k vs ~50k)
tradeoffs: Not compatible with existing Huffman bitstreams. 8-bit probabilities with 32-bit carryless arithmetic; under 1 KB for a 0-order model. Tiny scope (adaptive order-0 only).
caveats: First-party README claim in three bullet points. No benchmark code, corpus, compiler, flags or CPU stated. Baseline is a game-engine adaptive Huffman, not a general incumbent such as zlib Huffman or Huff0. Repo has only 3 commits (May-June 2022). Repo holds both qbc.c and qbc.cpp; language shown as C++ with a C version.
found_via: Blogs / talks: WebSearch 'range coder adaptive binary arithmetic coding fast open source library benchmark faster than LZMA rc github'
